## Reviews
- Code review followed compiler symbols across aliases and property declarations, verified cycle termination and ambiguous-value rejection, and reran the real endpoint join. No finding remained open.
- Security review confirmed the analyzer never executes target expressions and adds no write or rendering surface; the dependency audit is clean.
- Simplification review confirmed one recursive compiler-backed string resolver serves route and client discovery without repository-specific parsing.

## Deviations from plan
- The source configuration object is declared with `const` but its JavaScript properties are not deeply immutable. The analyzer records its single source initializer as a static configuration fact; it still rejects mutable identifier declarations, cycles, calls, and ambiguous declarations.

## Discovered issues
- none

## Open risks
- Code that mutates a configured object property after initialization can make the source initializer differ from runtime. Such code would appear as an assignment not modeled by this deliberately narrow resolver.
- No additional open implementation risk was found in local, real-repository, or hosted verification.
